title: TouchScale: 500 Hours of Vision and Touch for Robots

beats.text: Before you deploy your next physical policy, see how TouchScale unlocks 57.5% better precision.
beats.visual_focus: A robotic gripper fumbling and crushing a simple plastic cup.

beats.text: The villain is visual-only training, leaving robots blind to the friction and pressure of the physical world.
beats.visual_focus: A split screen showing a camera feed vs. a pressure-sensitive tactile map.

beats.text: TouchScale breaks this wall by capturing 500 hours of synchronized egocentric video and dense bimanual tactile data.
beats.visual_focus: A timeline showing 500 hours of synchronized data streams.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—it hit a real pain point in robotics that I've seen in labs. I didn't swipe because it didn't sound like a lecture. However, in Beat 4, you threw 'cross-modal transformer' at me. I know what a transformer is, but 'cross-modal' is a bit vague without a quick nod to how it's actually aligning the data streams. Also, 'massive leap for embodied intelligence' is bordering on buzzword territory, but it's acceptable since you backed it up with actual percentage gains.

thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Scaling physical supervision through unified human-sensor data

Everyone thought standard methods were enough, until TouchScale proved: recent visual-tactile datasets provide this missing supervision, but their synchronized tactile data remain far smaller in volume than human video.

Before you deploy your next architecture, consider this: Large-scale egocentric human interaction data is becoming an important source of physical supervision for embodied learning, yet video alone leaves the contact and pressure that characterize physical interaction unrecorded.
